Create a new legend

Source: R/method_Legend.R
create_legend.Rd

Create a new legend automatically for a column in a [sf::st_sf()] object.

Usage

create_legend(x, column, units = NULL, palette = "viridis", type = NULL)

Arguments

x

[sf::st_sf()] object.

column

`character` value with name of column.

units

`character` value containing the units for the values in the underlying data. Defaults to a `NULL` value.

palette

`character` value with the color palette. In particular, `palette` can be the name of a color palette that is recognized by [color_palette()]. Alternatively, it can be a set of hex color code delimited by semicolons (e.g., `palette = "#000000;#DDDDDD;#123456"`).

type

`character` value indicating if legend should be `"continuous"` `"categorical"`, `"presence/absence"`, or `"presence". Defaults to `NULL`, such that the legend type will be determined automatically.

Value

A new [new_continuous_legend()] or [new_categorical_legend()] object.

See also

Other method: create_dataset_from_sf(), create_solution(), create_solution_from_prioritization(), create_solution_legend(), create_tile_from_dataset(), create_tile_from_sf(), new_dataset(), tool_generated_provenance()

Examples

# simulate spatial data
sim_data <- simulate_spatial_data()
#> Error in simulate_spatial_data(): could not find function "simulate_spatial_data"

# create object
x <- create_legend(sim_data, "cost", units = "USD", palette = "PuBu")
#> Error in create_legend(sim_data, "cost", units = "USD", palette = "PuBu"): could not find function "create_legend"

# preview object
print(x)
#> Error: object 'x' not found
